evidence.intree_statement: Class TAlgebra `(T : C ⟶ C) `{@Monad C T} (a : C) := { t_alg : T a ~> a; t_id : t_alg ∘ ret ≈ id; t_action : t_alg ∘ fmap t_alg ≈ t_alg ∘ join }.
Class TAlgebraHom `(T : C ⟶ C) `{@Monad C T} (a b : C) (F : TAlgebra T a) (G : TAlgebra T b) := { t_alg_hom : a ~> b; t_alg_hom_commutes : t_alg_hom ∘ t_alg[F] ≈ t_alg[G] ∘ fmap[T] t_alg_hom }.

Program Definition EilenbergMoore `(T : C ⟶ C) `{H : @Monad C T} : Category := {| obj := ∃ a : C, @TAlgebra C T H a; hom := fun x y => TAlgebraHom T ``x ``y (projT2 x) (projT2 y); id := fun _ => {| t_alg_hom := id |}; compose := fun _ _ _ f g => {| t_alg_hom := t_alg_hom[f] ∘ t_alg_hom[g] |} |}.   (* the obligations prove identities and composites are again algebra maps *)

statement_record.book: A T-algebra is (A, α) with α : TA → A satisfying 1_A = α ∘ η_A and α ∘ μ_A = α ∘ Tα (eq. 10.5); a morphism h : (A,α) → (B,β) is h : A → B with h ∘ α = β ∘ T(h); identities and composites are inherited from C, so these form a category.
statement_record.intree: TAlgebra: t_alg : T a ~> a with t_id : t_alg ∘ ret ≈ id and t_action : t_alg ∘ fmap t_alg ≈ t_alg ∘ join. TAlgebraHom: t_alg_hom with t_alg_hom_commutes : t_alg_hom ∘ t_alg[F] ≈ t_alg[G] ∘ fmap[T] t_alg_hom. EilenbergMoore assembles them into a Category with identities and composites inherited from C.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same — the two algebra laws and the homomorphism square match exactly (t_action is Awodey's α∘μ_A = α∘Tα with the two sides swapped, an equation, so no loss), and the categoricity clause is discharged by the EilenbergMoore Program obligation using fmap_comp exactly as Awodey indicates.

verifier.notes: Blind pass found Monad/Algebra.v independently. Lines 24 and 44 verified, quotes verbatim and complete. t_id : t_alg ∘ ret ≈ id is Awodey's 1_A = α ∘ η_A; t_action : t_alg ∘ fmap t_alg ≈ t_alg ∘ join is his α ∘ μ_A = α ∘ Tα with the sides transposed (an equation — no loss). t_alg_hom_commutes is h ∘ α = β ∘ T(h) verbatim. The 'these form a category' clause is EilenbergMoore (Monad/Eilenberg/Moore.v:44) with the composite-is-a-homomorphism obligation at :51-58 pasting the two squares via fmap_comp, exactly as Awodey indicates; identities and composition are inherited from C on carriers and hom-equivalence is equivalence of underlying arrows. No same-name-weaker variant (grep 'TAlgebra' shows Monad/Algebra.v is the sole definition site; Structure/Coalgebra and Construction/FAlg are ENDOFUNCTOR algebras, a different notion Awodey himself separates in 10.5). Both files registered.

evidence.intree_statement: Program Definition EM_Adjunction : EM_Free ⊣ EM_Forget := @Build_Adjunction' (EilenbergMoore T) C EM_Free EM_Forget EM_adj_iso _ _.

Program Definition EM_Free : C ⟶ EilenbergMoore T := {| fobj := fun a => (T a; {| t_alg := @join C T H a |}); fmap := fun x y f => {| t_alg_hom := fmap[T] f |} |}.   (* obligations: join_ret and join_fmap_join give the algebra laws of (T a, μ_a); join_fmap_fmap gives the homomorphism square for F h = T h *)
Program Definition EM_Forget : EilenbergMoore T ⟶ C := {| fobj := fun a => `1 a; fmap := fun _ _ f => t_alg_hom[f] |}.   (* U(A,α) = A, U(h) = h *)
Theorem EM_Monad_agrees : EM_Forget ◯ EM_Free ≈ T.
Lemma EM_join_agrees {x : C} : fmap[EM_Forget] (@counit _ _ _ _ EM_Adjunction (EM_Free x)) ≈ join[T].   (* U ε F = μ: the induced monad is the original one *)

statement_record.book: C^T has T-algebras as objects and their morphisms as arrows, with U^T(A,α) = A, F^T C = (TC, μ_C), F^T h = Th; the unit is η, the counit is ε_(A,α) = α, both triangle identities hold, so F^T ⊣ U^T with U^T ∘ F^T = T and Uε F = μ.
statement_record.intree: EilenbergMoore T (the category, Monad/Eilenberg/Moore.v:44), EM_Forget, EM_Free, EM_Adjunction : EM_Free ⊣ EM_Forget, with EM_unit_agrees, EM_counit_agrees, EM_join_agrees and EM_Monad_agrees.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same — every component of the construction is a separate in-tree definition or lemma with the same formulas. The adjunction is built through the hom-setoid transposition isomorphism EM_adj_iso (restriction along η / extension by α ∘ T f) rather than by verifying the two triangles directly; that is the equivalent hom-set presentation, and the triangle identities are then available as the derived corollaries of Theory/Adjunction.v.

evidence.intree_statement: Instance list_Monad : Monad list := { ret := λ _ x, [x]; bind := λ _ _ x f, flatten (map f x) }.   (* η = singleton, join = flatten = concatenation of a list of lists *)

Program Definition Mon : Category := {| obj := { x : C & Monoid x }; hom := fun X Y => { f : `1 X ~> `1 Y & MonoidHom `2 X `2 Y f }; ... |}.   (* with Mon_Forget : Mon ⟶ C at line 93 and Mon_Forget_Faithful at line 101 *)

statement_record.book: For the free-monoid adjunction F : Sets ⇄ Mon : U, the induced monad on Sets is T(X) = lists over X with η the singleton and μ the concatenation of a list of lists; a T-algebra is exactly a monoid structure on its carrier, every monoid gives one and every T-algebra arises from a unique monoid, so Sets^T is (equivalent to) Mon.
statement_record.intree: list_Monad supplies the list monad's OPERATIONS over Coq types (ret = singleton, bind = flatten ∘ map, so join = flatten = concatenation); Mon is the category of internal monoids in a monoidal C with its faithful forgetful functor Mon_Forget : Mon ⟶ C.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker on every clause. (a) list_Monad instantiates Theory/Coq/Monad.v's Class Monad, which the file's own header states carries ONLY the operations — 'the laws are NOT recorded as fields here' — so the monad laws for list are nowhere proved (Theory/Coq/Monad/Proofs.v proves IsMonad only for Identity, arrow, and composites, not list). (b) It lives over Coq/Type, not Sets, and is not an instance of the categorical Theory/Monad.v Monad. (c) The Mon side exists only as a category with a forgetful functor — no left adjoint.

gap: Missing: (1) the free-monoid adjunction Sets ⇄ Mon (an exhaustive scan of every in-tree `⊣` construction turns up no free/forgetful adjunction into an algebraic category); (2) the list monad as a lawful categorical monad on Sets (or on Coq) — the only in-tree list monad is against the deliberately law-free Theory/Coq/Monad.v class; (3) the correspondence T-algebra ⇄ monoid in either direction; (4) the conclusion Sets^T ≃ Mon. The nearest in-tree analogue is Theory/Multicategory/Algebra.v's Comm_algebra_CMon (Comm-OPERAD algebras in Sets ⇄ commutative monoids, both directions, lines 523/673/686), which is a different theorem: operad rather than monad, and commutative monoids rather than monoids. Instance/Coq/Lists.v's list_initial shows list A is the initial ListF-ALGEBRA (endofunctor algebra), which Awodey himself flags in 10.5 as a distinct notion.

verifier.notes: MY BLIND PASS REACHED ABSENT AND WAS WRONG — I truncated an `rg ... | head -20` and missed Theory/Algebra/Monoid/Hom.v; the classifier's find is real. Verified: `Program Definition Mon : Category` at Theory/Algebra/Monoid/Hom.v:83 (cited line exact), Mon_Forget at :93, Mon_Forget_Faithful at :101, file registered in _CoqProject line 390. Also verified Theory/Coq/List.v:113 `Instance list_Monad : Monad list := { ret := λ _ x, [x]; bind := λ _ _ x f, flatten (map f x) }` — quote verbatim. PARTIAL is defensible and the strength_comparison is scrupulously honest about the three ways it is weaker; I independently confirmed each: (a) this `Monad` is Theory/Coq/Monad.v:32's law-free class whose own header says 'the laws are NOT recorded as fields here', and Theory/Coq/Monad/Proofs.v establishes IsMonad only for Identity, arrow and Compose — I grepped, list is not among them; (b) it lives over Coq/Type, not Sets, and is not a Theory/Monad.v Monad; (c) `Mon C {M}` is internal monoids in a MONOIDAL C (never instantiated at Sets in-tree), and the only functor is the forgetful one — grep for a left adjoint / free-monoid functor returns nothing, and Instance/CMon.v likewise has only CMon_Forget:169 with no free functor. So all four of Awodey's clauses (the adjunction, the lawful list monad, the algebra⇄monoid correspondence, Sets^T ≃ Mon) are missing and the gap field says so. This sits at the ABSENT/PARTIAL boundary; PARTIAL is the fairer call because the two ingredient objects Awodey names — the list monad's operations (η = singleton, μ = flatten, matching literally) and the category Mon with its forgetful functor — do exist in-tree.
